_comment: Documented synthetic values, permitted by scripts/privacy-scan.mjs. This is an ALLOWLIST, not
a denylist: anything matching a personal-data class and absent from here is reported. That
direction matters. A denylist would have to contain this machine's real values -- which is the
violation it exists to prevent -- and would still miss the next contributor's.
THIS FILE IS SCANNED BY THE SCANNER. Never write a complete forbidden-shaped value here, not even
as an example: describe it, or spell it with angle-bracket placeholders. Review round 8 found 25
such self-violations across the scanner, this config and the tests.
Adding an entry is a deliberate act. Add the synthetic value you introduced; never add a real one
to silence a finding.
accounts: matched by EXACT EQUALITY, never by prefix. Applies to the delimited path forms, where
the separator marks the account boundary exactly. Entries must be COLLISION-RESISTANT: the
scanner cannot tell a fixture using an allowed name from a contributor whose real account has the
same name, so a generic token here silently exempts a real person's home path. Review round 9
removed 'alice', 'bob', 'someone', 'user', 'example', 'runner', 'me', 'u' and 'x' for exactly
that reason. Only names no real account would plausibly carry belong here.
mangledHomePatterns: EXACT complete mangled project directories, enumerated one by one. Claude
Code's mangling is lossy -- the hyphen is both separator and a legal account character -- so the
account boundary cannot be recovered from the mangled string. An earlier version anchored the
pattern but left an optional '(-anything)?' tail, which is prefix allowlisting wearing anchors:
it cleared a run whose account could equally have been '<declared>-<something-else>'. There is no
pattern that resolves the ambiguity, so nothing is inferred and each real fixture path is listed.
Adding a fixture project directory means adding a line here, which is the intended friction.
sessionIdPatterns / workflowIdPatterns: ANCHORED regular expressions matching a COMPLETE
identifier, never a prefix -- prefix allowlisting accepted a synthetic prefix followed by
arbitrary real-looking hex. The 019c0000- family is this repo's convention for fabricated Codex
rollout ids: it keeps the UUIDv7 shape so fixtures exercise real parsing, and the pattern pins the
zero padding that makes it obviously fake.
emailDomains: domains non-deliverable by standard (RFC 2606) or by convention.
binaryExtensions: files whose bytes cannot be text-scanned. Anything binary and NOT listed here
is reported as unscannable rather than skipped, because a silent skip is how a scan reports clean
without having looked.
